name: ACSPerf'
description: An ECU remapping "file service" in Ners (Gard), France. Garages and tuners upload the original engine-computer read, pay in credits, choose options (performance, E85 conversion, etc.), and download the modified file. Installation is the customer's job (company-stated, per its terms). The homepage claims 3,000+ vehicles optimised and 50+ partner garages (company-stated). The ordering portal handles credits, file upload, order chat, deferred monthly payment for partners, and an accountant view with FEC export; its agency described this in a case study. Founded Aug 2025, FR, two founders on TrustMRR.

mentions.evidence: MRR $0 (credit purchases, not subscriptions), ~$30,913 L30 (+79.5%), ~$73,115 last 3 months, ~$240,392 last 12 months, ~$262,480 all-time, ~90% L30 profit margin. Revenue synced Oct 8, 2026 ~07:40 Warsaw (05:40 UTC).
mentions.indieAngle: Don't do the tuning. Sell the portal: a white-label "file service" SaaS for the many small ECU tuners who still take files over email and WhatsApp. It needs credits, upload, order status, partner pricing and invoices/exports, at a monthly fee per tuner. It's plain Next.js/Supabase/Stripe CRUD, and every tuner with resellers needs one.

whyItPrints: It's a B2B digital-file business with no stock. Pro tuners send files every week, and each file is paid for in pre-bought credits. L30 is up 79.5% and the margin is 90%. Caveat: its own terms note that remapping counts as a "transformation notable" under the French road code, and some options it lists (EGR/DPF/AdBlue changes) are a regulatory risk area in the EU.
